summary: PASS. The frozen candidate is a compact but substantive binary-record parsing/evaluation utility. All major runtime modules are reachable from /app/equiv/bin/equiv-eval, and layout metadata drives byte sizing, COMP-3 representation, REDEFINES aliasing, ODO traversal, record-boundary progression, report invariants, and process exit behavior. The implementation is far below strict large-system scale, but this review is explicitly non-strict; within that profile the difficulty is concentrated in real domain invariants and state transitions rather than LOC, duplicated modules, generated filler, or verifier-only behavior. No material unreachable padding, cloned subsystem, giant lookup-table shortcut, or constant-output production shell was found.

evidence.observation: Q6 requires reachability, material branching/state/error behavior, differentiated responsibilities, meaningful data/state, cross-module partial-fix traps, a removal test, and domain-derived rather than padded complexity; the >=3,000 substantive LOC condition is stated only for large_system_strict.

The Q6 method requires tracing entrypoints, module reachability/responsibility, clone/wrapper/filler risk, cross-module invariants, ~25% removal impact, data-to-branch relevance, and separation of substantive runtime logic from noise.
The operator entrypoint resolves the installed /app/equiv tree, sets PYTHONPATH, and directly executes python3 -m src.cli; it is a thin legitimate launcher rather than a substitute for runtime logic.
The CLI exposes layout/records/output operator inputs, loads the layout, reads binary records, invokes evaluation, persists the JSON report, and maps aggregate error state to process exit status.

The layout module performs stateful interpretation of PIC forms, signedness, scale, COMP-3 metadata, REDEFINES targeting, and ODO group boundaries into typed Pic/Odo/Layout structures consumed by the runtime.

Record parsing maintains a byte cursor, derives field widths from layout metadata, branches between display and packed fields, iterates nested ODO fields, and returns partial state plus record-length/error information. The starter defects are on this live path, not isolated benchmark-only functions.

Evaluation repeatedly consumes unpacked record length to locate the next concatenated record and derives packed-value, ODO-length, and REDEFINES invariants from parsed state; these results feed the externally written report and CLI success/failure behavior.

The shipped layout combines fixed text/display fields, signed scaled COMP-3, unsigned COMP-3, REDEFINES aliasing, and a bounded OCCURS DEPENDING ON group, so one record boundary depends on multiple interacting layout semantics.

The representative binary state is 72 bytes and materially exercises the layout rather than padding it: it contains two concatenated SKU records whose expected lengths differ because the first has an ODO occurrence and the second has zero, while packed fields include positive and negative sign cases.

The solver-visible operational contract ties COMP-3 nibble/sign/scale rules, REDEFINES non-advancing offsets, ODO-dependent lengths, concatenated record boundaries, and the emitted report schema to the same evaluator workflow.

The incident evidence describes hex-rendered packed values, max-span ODO consumption, REDEFINES offset drift, and lost negative sign; each symptom corresponds to an actually reachable path in the starter rather than an unrelated narrative subsystem.

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: Compact and well below the large_system_strict 3,000-LOC threshold, but this task is explicitly non-strict. The substantive runtime is concentrated in four small Python modules plus a thin shell entrypoint; almost every runtime branch participates in layout interpretation, record decoding, state/error propagation, or report generation. No generated, vendored, comment-heavy, duplicate-resource, or unreachable module volume is being used to manufacture scale.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Operator-facing orchestration, input/output paths, report persistence, and exit semantics.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: Consumes evaluator summary error_count to determine process success; file/layout failures propagate as runtime failures.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Parse the compact COBOL-layout DSL into typed field, scale, sign, REDEFINES, and ODO metadata.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: Maintains pending REDEFINES and current ODO parse state; rejects unknown field syntax.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Decode one variable-length binary record using layout metadata and return parsed fields, consumed byte length, and error.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: Maintains the byte cursor across fixed and repeated fields; parsing exceptions return partial fields plus an error/length boundary.

MAJOR_MODULES.responsibility: Walk concatenated records, validate domain invariants, aggregate per-record state, and construct the public equivalence report.
MAJOR_MODULES.state_error_behavior: Uses each consumed record length to advance global offset and tracks signed/ODO/REDEFINES health across all records.

PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Correct COMP-3 conversion alone still leaves REDEFINES cursor drift and ODO max-span consumption capable of corrupting record boundaries.
Correct REDEFINES aliasing alone still leaves ODO count handling able to consume bytes belonging to the next concatenated record.
Correct ODO traversal alone still leaves packed sign/scale semantics and unsigned-F versus signed-C/D validation incorrect.
Layout parsing, byte-width calculation, unpack cursor state, report invariants, and CLI exit behavior are linked, so a locally plausible parser patch can remain globally wrong.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing roughly one major runtime module (about a quarter of the compact core) materially destroys behavior: without layout parsing the evaluator cannot interpret field semantics; without unpacking it cannot derive fields/record lengths; without report evaluation it loses multi-record progression, domain invariant aggregation, report construction, and the CLI success/failure signal. The removable pieces are support documentation/data, not fake core code.
